notes_list.title: Amine Functional Group Tests
notes_list.basic_overview: Amines are basic nitrogen compounds; their qualitative behavior includes acid-base salt formation, nucleophilicity and characteristic derivatization.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Primary, secondary and tertiary amines differ in substitution pattern and in reactions such as sulfonylation/Hinsberg-type analysis. Nitrous acid chemistry can further distinguish classes.
notes_list.examples: RNH2 + HCl → RNH3+Cl−; primary aromatic amines can form diazonium salts under cold acidic nitrite conditions.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Nitrous acid is generated in situ from NaNO2 + mineral acid, commonly at low temperature for diazotization of aromatic primary amines.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Acid-base protonation is fast. In derivatization, nucleophilic attack at sulfur or diazonium-forming nitrosation pathways can differentiate amine classes.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Observed rate depends on protonation state; excessive acid can reduce nucleophilicity of amines.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Core for qualitative analysis and aromatic amine chemistry.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not perform aromatic diazotization at uncontrolled high temperature; diazonium salts have condition-dependent stability.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
